content: A 100-tonne all-terrain crane might command a certain daily rate for a short-term hire, but this rate can fluctuate based on regional demand. For instance, if several large construction projects are running concurrently in Gauteng, rates for this class of crane may increase. The most significant pricing power lies with large-capacity cranes. Due to their scarcity, a 500-tonne or 750-tonne crane can command premium rates, especially for urgent or highly specialized projects. The supply-demand balance for these assets is critical; there may only be a handful of such cranes available in the entire country at any given time. A company that owns one and has it available when a major mine shutdown or wind farm project requires it is in a very strong negotiating position. Fleet intelligence requires Veralift to continuously monitor these market rates through its own quoting activity, feedback from clients, and informal industry networks to ensure its pricing is both competitive and profitable. This intelligence allows the commercial team to know when they can hold firm on price and when they need to be more flexible to secure utilization. Ultimately, a sophisticated fleet strategy, informed by deep market intelligence, enables Veralift to deploy the right assets, to the right projects, at the right price, maximizing its return on investment.
